title: Remapped Keyboard Shortcut Causing a Problem to Other Keys: Existing Issue

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a video/archive, confirmed that disabling Keyboard Manager clears the problem, and described a concrete Alt+C/Alt+V followed by Delete sequence. This is actionable for a maintainer-side reproduction; do not request another diagnostic bundle.
evidence: The issue includes an attached ZIP and video.
The reporter says disabling Keyboard Manager restores the affected keys.
The comments provide an Alt+C/Alt+V, then Delete sequence as a way to reproduce the interaction.
judgment.recommended_action: Replay the exact reported shortcut sequence with the attachment's mapping in an isolated profile and trace key state if the symptom reproduces.

fix_assessment.rationale: The on/off correlation and sequence justify reproduction, but the exact event path and failure state have not been established sufficiently to select a code fix.

issue_context.summary: A Keyboard Manager remapped shortcut reportedly disrupts other key behavior; the reporter supplied a video and a repeatable Alt+C/Alt+V then Delete sequence.

inferences: The remap may leave a synthetic or physical modifier state inconsistent, but the exact affected key and transition must be observed before assigning a cause.
issue_context.analysis: Use the evidence already attached and reproduce in a clean environment. The immediate question is which key event fails and whether its down/up pair is balanced; generic requests for logs would add little.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all nine comments, including attachment references and the usable key sequence.
Reviewed KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp as the likely event path; no source finding confirms the specific failure.

reproduce.title: Test whether Alt+C/Alt+V disrupts subsequent Delete input
prerequisites: A clean profile containing only the mapping shown in the reporter's attachment.
A test editor with no unrelated shortcut or macro extensions.
steps: Verify the test editor accepts ordinary Alt+C, Alt+V, and Delete with Keyboard Manager disabled.
Enable only the issue's shortcut mapping and replay Alt+C, Alt+V, then Delete in the same focus context.
Repeat the sequence several times and note the exact key or text behavior that diverges.
If reproducible, trace modifier and Delete key down/up events, then compare with the same mapping disabled.
reproduce.expected_result: Delete and all modifiers retain their normal behavior after the remapped shortcut sequence, or the trace identifies the missing/extra transition.
